subsystems.name: Entry vehicle
subsystems.role: survives the high-speed entry into Venus's atmosphere and protects the payload.

subsystems.name: Descent system
subsystems.role: slows the probe to a controlled speed through the cloud deck.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: measures organic chemistry and cloud droplet composition directly.

subsystems.name: Avionics and power
subsystems.role: runs the instruments, stores data and manages the descent sequence.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: sends the measurements back to Earth during the short descent.

subsystems.name: Thermal and chemical protection
subsystems.role: keeps electronics within operating limits and resists sulfuric acid aerosols.

buildSteps.title: Define the science target
buildSteps.detail: Choose the altitude band in the Venus cloud deck where liquid droplets and organic chemistry are most likely.

buildSteps.title: Design the entry and descent profile
buildSteps.detail: Size the heat shield and parachute so the probe survives entry and reaches the target cloud layer at a useful speed.

buildSteps.title: Build and test the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Construct the fluorescence detector and droplet analyser, then validate them in laboratory chambers that mimic Venus temperature, pressure and acid chemistry.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the payload
buildSteps.detail: Fit the instruments, avionics, power and communications into the compact entry vehicle.

buildSteps.title: Environmental testing
buildSteps.detail: Subject the assembled probe to vibration, vacuum, thermal cycling and acid exposure to prove it can survive launch and descent.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Fly on a small dedicated launch vehicle and coast to Venus on a short interplanetary trajectory.

buildSteps.title: Entry and descent
buildSteps.detail: The probe enters the atmosphere, deploys its parachute and begins sampling cloud particles as it falls.

buildSteps.title: Measure and transmit
buildSteps.detail: Instruments record organic fluorescence and droplet properties, and the data are transmitted to Earth before the probe is destroyed by the environment.

prerequisites.why: laboratory prototypes exist, but none has yet flown through Venus's clouds.
past Venus missions carried larger probes; shrinking the heat shield, parachute and systems to small scale is unproven.
the cloud deck contains sulfuric acid and temperatures near 100 °C, which challenge lightweight electronics.
small rockets and compact cruise stages can now send small payloads on interplanetary trajectories.
a tiny probe's weak signal may need a relay orbiter or a very sensitive ground station.

pathway.milestone: laboratory validation of the organic detector and droplet analyser
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the instruments can identify organics in Venus-like droplets.

pathway.milestone: first flight of a small probe through the cloud deck
pathway.unlocks: the first direct measurements of cloud-layer organic chemistry and droplet composition.

pathway.milestone: follow-up probes with more capable instruments and longer descent
pathway.unlocks: isotopic and chemical detail to distinguish biological from abiotic chemistry.
laboratory analysis on Earth of material from the cloud deck.
